sections.skill: Use simulation results to judge a model

branch.new_demand: Read a distribution of simulated results to decide about a model.
branch.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the simulations the student can now run are summarized and compared with data.

questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A coin claimed to be fair gave 9 heads in 10 flips. Use the table of 100 simulated sets. Decision rule: if results at least as extreme as the observed result happen in fewer than 5% of the simulated trials, the model is not consistent with the data; otherwise it is consistent. Which decision is correct?
questions.prompt_markup: A coin claimed to be fair gave 9 heads in 10 flips. Use the table of 100 simulated sets. Decision rule: if results at least as extreme as the observed result happen in fewer than 5% of the simulated trials, the model is not consistent with the data; otherwise it is consistent. Which decision is correct?

choices.text: Not consistent: 9 or more heads happened in only 2% of the trials.
Not consistent: a fair coin must give exactly 5 heads.
Consistent: a fair coin can land heads 9 times.
Consistent: 9 or more heads happened in 2% of the trials.

questions.correct_answer: Not consistent: 9 or more heads happened in only 2% of the trials.
